cases.name: Shannon Marie Bigger
cases.about:
She was an intern at the Washington Adventist Hospital Foundation in Takoma Park as well as a member of the Seventh-Day Adventist Church. "She has such a trusting and loving personality. She could talk to anyone," said Kimberly King, who worked with Bigger at the foundation. "We've had plenty of conversations that this area is different from Walla Walla."

Rhodene Hubbard, Bigger's supervisor, described the intern as "very naive, very innocent. She had a personality and the energy to talk to anyone."

The oldest daughter of an assistant professor of religion and social work at Walla Walla College in College Place, Wash., the Seventh-Day Adventist facility where she graduated last year, Bigger dedicated her life to the church.

At the end of the month, she would have completed a one-year internship as a development assistant in the fund-raising department of the Takoma Park hospital. Her next job was to be in Caldwell, Idaho, where she planned to raise funds for a Seventh-Day Adventist high school.

Her college adviser, Nancy Semotiuk, described Bigger as "extremely friendly" and well known to the 1,700 students on the campus. "She simply would talk to anyone.
cases.narrative: On 6/17/1996, her body was found on her bed with multiple slashes on the neck. Police believe after meeting her briefly at a mall, he showed up at her door between 4 and 7 p.m. Sunday and she let him in.

cases.name: Denise Middleton
cases.about:
Middleton’s family told FOX 5 Denise was funny, witty, and loving and that she loved fashion, hair, and makeup. They say she was excited to become a mom and say they are heartbroken. 

The Middleton family released the following statement:
"Denise Middleton was a funny, witty, and loving person. She loved fashion, hair, and makeup. She could make an outfit out of anything. Her laugh was infectious and her jokes were the highlight of special moments. She was so excited to become a mom. She told everyone who would listen! Her heart was soooo big and she always made sure you knew she loved you.

Denise was a walking book of positive affirmations. She always said the nicest things about you when she saw you. Always complimenting someone and giving out love. If you had a disagreement with her, she would make sure to make things right. Denise was so loved by her family and so cared for! We are heartbroken that this was her story and reality. We wish our efforts would have brought her back home to us. Denise and Baby Ezekiel is loved and missed by the Middleton Family. Thank you all for your prayers and kind words! This has shaken our family up but has brought us even closer! We will make sure justice is served for her and baby Ezekiel #protectblackwomen"
cases.narrative:
Police discovered her body in an advanced state of decomposition when they went to his apartment to arrest him on an unrelated matter, and believe she was killed sometime in 10/2022. Officials said Moore fatally shot Middleton, likely shortly after entering his apartment complex on Oct. 9, 2022, following an argument that happened in an elevator. An autopsy found Middleton was shot seven times.

An hour later, security video showed Moore leave the apartment. Officials said he traveled the country for 26 days, and later returned to live with the decomposing bodies until his arrest on Dec. 9 of that year.
